text.p: Bonds ended off their highs on renewed fears that a U.S. rate rise may not be long delayed. Traders said that the longer end looked likely to hold to a 115 basis point spread with the German market on Wednesday.

End-users still have not returned to the market amidst continuing nervousness about a possible delay in the single currency, traders said. The Portuguese bond trend will be set by what happens abroad, particularly to the Bunds, they added.
"The market came back from its highs but I would bet on the 10-year cash staying at around 115 basis points above the Bund," said one trader.

"Tomorrow, the activity is likely to be pure trading but if the spread (with the Bund) goes over 120 basis points, I see strong buying interest if questions over the single currency does not flare again," said another trader. Traders said the short end was well supported, taking its cue from Spain where there was optimism about the inflation number for February.
The escudo closed little changed against the mark having ignored the more volatile behaviour of the peseta, traders said.
But some traders said that there could be a delayed reaction on Wednesday, with the escudo beginning to feel the weakness suffered by the peseta and the lira on Tuesday afternoon.
